# Smart office operations

## People interact with tools for change

|  |
| --- |
| The product concept shifted from “human adaptation tools” to “tool adaptation tools”. |

| Dimensions | Past: human adaptation tools | AI Age: Tools adapted to people |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interactive | Menu driver and memory command: User needs to know where the function is, remember complex shortcut keys and formula syntax (e.g. VLOOKUP). One-way, mechanical interaction. | Natural language dialogue: direct description of needs in daily languages, e.g. summary of Q3 procurement costs. Two-way, understanding interactive. |
| Goal achieved | Manual operations and step-by-step: Each operation requires a gradual user, starting from scratch and relying on the professional skills of the user. | Intended understanding and automated generation: Users propose targets, AI automatically executes a series of complex operations. |
| Processes and collaboration | Inflexible processes: collaborative processes are fixed, information is isolated and cross-application data requires manual handling. | AI Working stream understanding context: automatically generate minutes after meetings and distribute them to the person concerned; extract task items from mail and automatically add them to the to-do list. Tools proactively connect to workflows and break barriers to application. |
| Data processing and analysis | Dependence on expertise: Deep data analysis skills are required. Users must know what formula is used and which chart best reflects the value of the data, and the conclusions depend on manual discovery. | Smart Insight and Visualization: All users need is data, and AI can automatically analyse trends, detect anomalies, make assumptions and recommend appropriate visualization options. |
| Learning costs | One-size-fits-all interfaces and high learning costs: all users face the same interfaces and functions, with limited individualized settings; skilled use of advanced functionality requires long-term learning and training. | Self-adaptation interfaces and learning curves close to zero: AI learns user habits, prioritizes common functions, and thousands of people. |

# Reasons for purchase

## Purchase drivers depth analysis

### Functional drivers

#### Driver I: Turn data into end-to-end business stream

|  |
| --- |
| Clients are usually not “no software”, but rather too many software, forms and chat tools. The real purchase objective is to reduce duplicate entries and allow sales, procurement, warehousing, finance and management to work around the same data. |
| Corresponding product values: harmonized data model, cross-module trigger, API/database connection, business questions. |

#### Driver II: Rapid adaptation to non-standardized processes

|  |
| --- |
| The systems and operations of growing enterprises are still changing, and the traditional ERP two is slow and expensive, and the purely standard cloud service is not very relevant. Visualization brings not “development for all” as a core value, but rather a change in business that does not wait in line for IT. |
| Corresponding product values: forms, processes, reports, portals, templates and custom operations. |

#### Driver III: Let AI move from "response to questions" to "implementation"

|  |
| --- |
| Businesses ' new sense of universal chat robots has declined and are more willing to pay for automatic filing, filling, generating quotations, triggering approvals, forecasting inventories and synchronizing assignments. |
| Corresponding product value: Job intelligence, AI CRM, procurement request price, meeting to-do, cross-system implementation. |

#### Driver IV: Security and control

|  |
| --- |

## Text
In 2025, the cloud conference was not an “option”, but a “just-in-demand tool” for cross-regional collaboration among enterprises.

Just like sales in your team, you have to go online every day to connect clients -- talk about needs, demonstrate programs, keep an eye on the project. However, as the number of clients increases and the demand becomes more complex, it is also necessary to bring together internal teams; together with outreach abroad, meetings with clients in different languages are slowly becoming a burden:

Before we start, we're going to have to go through the information, manage the issues, build the meetings manually, and send the links to people in mainstream social tools, mainstream business platforms, mailing lists, 30 minutes of meetings, one hour of preparation; either we can't communicate in depth, or we can't keep track of the information, we can't keep track of it, we can't catch up with the top, we're always afraid of missing key content; we're going to have a recording, we're going to spend almost 100 hours a month, we're going to spend all day a week, we're going to have to follow up on it; let's not mention that the network is running into “PPT”, or we're worried about the leak of business meetings.

These problems can be solved easily by Kuailu Meeting.

As an AI-based smart meeting system, Kuailu Technology integrates AI and audio and video technology, which provides remote communication collaboration and information management services, such as the core functions of AI conference hosting, AI minutes, human image digital person, conference recording, and somatic recognition, multi-channel voice separation, intelligent search backtracking, which can be covered by daily meetings, remote training or online interviews. It also supports narrow-banded high-resolution video, with public clouds, privatization deployments and adaptation to different business needs.

I. Pre-session time is not required: a word can be used to organize meetings, and an invitation is accurate. Power.

Previously, at the preparatory meeting, you had to go through a collection of materials to keep the subject of the meeting in line, build a meeting in the system manually, and finally send links to participants scattered across mainstream social tools, mainstream corporate office platforms, and telephone addresses. A 30-minute meeting could take one hour to prepare alone, particularly affecting efficiency.

Now, using Kuailu Meeting, you can just talk to the system and ask for it, without manually filling in any meeting information, and AI will automatically set up your meetings and give you notice. It also supported real-time transitions in Chinese and English where overseas colleagues or clients were present, pre-communications would not be carded and preparatory efficiency would be raised directly.

II. There is no fear of omission: digital person, AI hosting + real-time translation, full information control

Have you ever had these problems with important meetings? There are several meetings at a senior level, which are so fragmented that other people's representatives are afraid of missing key messages; meetings with overseas clients, who don't know the language, and it's hard enough to think about what they say, can't talk business properly.

Kuailu Meeting offers specific solutions to these problems:

• Allowing companies to customize executive-specific digital or 3D-styles, through ASI face-catching techniques, allowing digital faces to be synchronized with participants in real time, allowing them to participate in meetings without exposing their true identity, protecting executive privacy, matching 3D digital corporate styles, and enhancing brand recognition.

• If there are too many meetings of senior managers or if there are any temporary departures, the AI hosting function can take over the management of the meetings, even if the time is scattered, and many meetings can be easily handled; and the minutes of the meetings during the hosting period can be accurately reviewed by the senior managers, without missing any key information.

• Cross-country communication is much better, as it supports real-time translation in more than a dozen languages, such as Central, British, Thai and Malay. You do not have to focus on translation, focus on the content of meetings, and communicate efficiently.

After the meeting, no effort was made: AI automatically wrote the minutes and the process moved faster.

More operations and more online meetings followed, with many teams meeting almost 100 times a month. It will take at least a full day per week to organize the proceedings into a detailed summary. It is also prone to errors, either missing key messages or a lack of timely follow-up to the conclusions of the meetings, which has a significant impact on progress.

Kuailu Meeting, with its unique conference room voice recognition technology, is able to accurately match each speaker and increase the accuracy of the proceedings by 50 per cent; it is also able to customize the business-specific summary template, which took three hours to write, and is now available in 15 minutes, resulting in faster outcomes and less time for transactional work.

IV. Special needs are met: network stability, security and safety

It is now normal for meetings to be held at any time or place, but the network environment is different from one place to another, and unstable signals affect the effectiveness of meetings. Kuailu Meeting reduces the demand for broadband by optimizing coding technology, and can hold a steady video conference regardless of the network environment; and it supports 1080 P-high-screen, 150 ms low delay, with a 50 per cent passback resistance to shaking, with a clear and stable picture of the entire process and no “PPT”.

If your meeting involves business secrets and concerns about leaking information, Kuailu Meeting ' s privatization deployment function will be useful. The deployment through privatization would ensure the security of meetings and prevent the disclosure of information, and would allow all information generated by the meetings to be owned by enterprises without addressing the issue of attribution of data.

Now online meetings are no longer a tool for simple connectivity, but rather a movement towards "AI, smart, secure, scenery" -- • Business needs to move away from “meetings” to “meetings and transformations” to address both the efficiency of cross-border collaboration and barriers to cross-border communication, and to ensure that information security and results are achieved.

Kuailu Meeting responds to this trend and integrates AI in depth into the whole process: breaking communication barriers with smart grouping, real-time translation, using digital and AI hosting solutions points, accelerating the translation of results with smart records, and ensuring experience and security with a narrow belt of high-level, privatized deployments. It does not just help businesses “to meet efficiently”, it is better able to upgrade through the intellectualization of the entire chain of meetings, making each conference a “productivity tool” for business and enabling decision-making, and truly empowering firms to take the lead in working together.

## Text
Operating alone, a $5 million regenerative resource company with a monthly flow of water, a 5 per cent control deviation in the acquisition pricing could result in a hidden loss of $250,000 in a single purchase chain. Kuailu Technology argued that price gaps were only the tip of a roughly managed iceberg, and that management problems such as inefficient turnover of stocks, poor customer accounting, fiscal compliance risks and production control irregularities would continue to affect business profits.

Industry development has long since left the savagery of “the more you earn” and digital transformation has become the core of corporate resilience to cyclical risks and the construction of profit barriers. The digital transformation of the deep tiller resource industry of Kuailu Technology, focal recovery, sorting, resource-based processing, full chain pain point, has led to many head lithium recovery, steel recovery head transformations, and below is a combination of the two hot track cases of scrap motor vehicles and lithium recovery, with digital landing values and landing paths.

End-of-life motor vehicles & scrap steel recycling: fine upgrading of the compliance industry

The end-of-life market for motor vehicles is breaking out when the old-for-new policy is adopted.

The traditional manual billing and verbal accounting of dismantling enterprises will be difficult to sustain because of retroactive non-compliance and non-retention of data, and digitization will be key to business compliance and sustainability.

In the case of a head end-of-life vehicle enterprise, the owner of the enterprise runs scrap motor vehicles, agricultural machine recycling and waste steel resource processing, dismantles more than 8000 scrap vehicles annually, more than 1,000 scrap agricultural machines, and 100 tons of scrap steel annual processing volume, which is the leading enterprise in the regional recycling economy.

As a typical waste steel recycling facility, the main management bottlenecks are the non-standardized material coding, the fragmentation of data, and the inability to meet the retroactive demand for downstream markets; and, secondly, the central dilemmas of output stocks, such as incalculability, and the lack of dynamic early warning mechanisms, also lead to incalculable cost-benefits, which seriously affect the speed of response to market fluctuations.

In response, the enterprise introduced a digital solution for the Kuailu + Regenerative Resources industry, which built an integrated control system for the mobile side plus the PC end, and provided access to the procurement warehouse, workshop dismantling, warehouse management, sales reconciliations, etc.

Mission-driven achievement of proactive business synergies and significant optimization of business targets after landing: reduction of time taken to trace materials of the whole class 83.33 per cent

Increased efficiency of cross-sectoral synergistic operations

55.56 per cent increase in inactive stock drive activity

Increased efficiency of workshop production 34.37 per cent

Dropping down core capacity

1. (a) One-yard full-chain traceability system: the raw materials vehicle automatically produces a unique identity code, the whole process is recorded in the bank, dismantled, released, sold and processed, and meets environmental requirements, taxes, multiple dimensions of end-of-life controls;

2. Classified smart stock alerts: multiple early warning labels for stock ceilings, floors, demurrage cycles, automatic system alerts to excess backlogs of goods and raw materials to avoid stock losses resulting from steel price fluctuations;

3. Dismantling BOM Intelligent Measurement: Enter a vehicle model, exit parameters automatically predetermine scrap steel after dismantling, spare parts output specifications and weights, pre-set pre-sale quotations, and change the lag pattern of the traditional full weight to account for costs.

Power cell recycling: fine regulation determines the enterprise ' s space

New energy vehicle stocks are rising year by year, power battery decommissioning cycles are concentrated, with about 350,000 tons decommissioned in 2025 and the main calibre of forecast retirements in 2030 at about 100-120 GWh. Mass decommissioned electric cores generate hundreds of billion-class urban mineral markets.

With the back-up management of the New Deal by power cells in the six sectors, the end-of-life of a car, the rigidity of a whole core tracer, the high external dependence of scarce metals, such as lithium nickel, and the continued strategic value of lithium resource recovery.

Under the track dividend, lithium recyclers still face multiple business challenges: Upstream recovery sources are fragmented, procurement offers are unorthodox, raw materials costs are affected by sharp fluctuations in lithium prices; production end dismantling processes are controlled, blending of inputs lacks standardized accounting tools, the whole process relies on spreadsheets, manual bookkeeping, half-finished products, cost-sharing of finished products is cumbersome and uneven; downstream environmental regulations are becoming increasingly stringent, informal small workshops are underpriced and formal plants often face shortages of raw materials when they are constrained by procurement costs.

The full-process fine-tuning of digitally becomes an important direction for an enterprise. In the case of a lithium lead company with Kuailu, its main focus lithium batteries were recycled and dismantled, through the digitized platform Kuailu, through procurement tests, warehousing, production dismantling, cost sharing, customer settlement of all six business scenarios, and close-ring control of more than 20 subdivisions of business lines, resulting in:

Cost accounting is manual: material costs are automatically aggregated, multi-finished costs are automatically shared, and cost accounting efficiency and accuracy are significantly increased.

Compliance is integrated retroactively and policy requirements are met: Through the whole process of "Procedure for recycling production and sale of finished products", systematic recording of data at all stages, generation of retroactive reports, full compliance with policy requirements for full life cycle traceability, and evasion of compliance risks.

Kuailu ' s three core program advantages, enabling corporate long-term growth

In line with policy trends, the Kuailu AI+ Intellectual Solutions for the Regenerative Resources Industry, based on industry experience in deep-drive farming, can be sensibly weighed at the top of the ground, smart parks, closed doors, revenue billing, OA multi-type third-party systems, break the isolation of software and hardware data, one-stop coverage from raw materials to finished products, with the following three major features:

AI Depth embedding into the factory overpound, storage streaming, production discharge, relying on visual recognition + industry big data, intelligent pre-dismantling into material volume, connecting large commodity intelligence data to feed reference prices, helping enterprises to adjust their procurement tempo flexibly, and reducing the risk of raw material price fluctuations.

2 | batch bar code global retroactive, no concerns about compliance

A two-coding control system that allows full chain tracing of raw materials sources, workshop processing, finished stock, automatic archiving of accounts, easy response to regulatory needs such as environmental audits, tax verification, back-to-back platform reporting, etc., and circumventing compliance penalties from the root causes.

3-year-old industry customized products, adapted to break down the demand for tracks

Customization of BOM models for end-of-life vehicles, agricultural machinery, lithium electricity, etc., supports customized development based on product-specific smart output data, taking into account the light-quantified up-line requirements of small and medium-sized processing plants and the deep deployment of multi-united plants.

From purchasing smart prices, over-pounding, stock dynamics alerts, full chain tracking, one-key accounting, operating data boards, six core scenarios digitally landed, helping regenerative resource enterprises to move completely out of empirical management constraints.

In an environment of strong industry regulation and increased stock competition, digitization has moved from an enterprise’s options for upgrading to a need to cross the industry. In the future, Kuailu Technology continues to be an iterative AI digital product, helping to increase the number of recycling enterprises moving from rough operations to refined intelligence operations, moving from passive compliance to active profit growth.

# Disable expression by law and public content

## National level, highest level, best type of term

| --- |
| In principle, the following expressions are not used to market goods or services: |
| Express terms of the law: national, highest, best. |
| Absolute advocacy equivalent to or highly comparable to national products, national brands, world-class, world-highest, global top, top, top, top, most advanced, front, most advanced, most advanced, most professional, most secure, most reliable, most accurate, fastest, cheapest, most worthwhile, most extreme, top, most peak, ultimate, absolute ahead, unmatched. |
| The country's first, global first, industry first, No.1, TOP 1, brand 1, market share first, sales first, unique, exclusive, first, first, first, first, first, leading, industry poles, and far ahead. |
| Unproven authoritative expression: State certification, State designation, government designation, official accreditation, certification of authority, exclusiveness of State organs, specialty, specialty. |
| In the case of official awards, qualifications, rank, fixed title or a limited range of verifiable facts, the words “highest” “first” “national” may reasonably appear. Such expressions should accurately refer to full, objective facts and scope of application and should not be extended to propaganda conclusions. |

## Absolute impact, security and zero risk commitment

|  |
| --- |
| Absolute effects: 100 per cent effective, 100 per cent accurate, complete, definitive, one-off, immediate, permanent, no error, zero error, zero failure, no loss. |
| Absolute safety: 100% safety, absolute safety, zero risk, zero risk, never-ending, never-discovery, no risk, full confidentiality. |
| It is absolutely applicable: it applies to the owner, to any enterprise, to the whole scene, without any conditions, to the zero threshold, to the zero cost of learning, to the complete exemption from maintenance. |
| Absolute commitment: guarantees of success, success of the package, inclusion, satisfaction, unconditional refunds (if inconsistent with the actual provisions), certainty, necessity, absolute, never. |
| It was suggested to replace the word “support” with “support” to “help” to supplement product versions, testing environments, service ranges or contractual terms, subject to agreed configuration and applicable conditions. |

## False credentials, endorsements and false images

|  |
| --- |
| Not obtained or expired but declared: State certification, authoritative certification, official partners, designated suppliers, recommendations from industry associations, accreditation by an institution. |
| :: The fraudulent or disguised use of the names or images of State organs, agents of State organs and violations of the flag, emblem, flag, emblem, etc. |
| The name, portrait, voice, evaluation, case, trademark, Logo or customer list is used without written consent for endorsement. |
| Fiction or exaggeration of patents, soft writing, awards, sales, number of clients, R & D inputs, team size, coverage areas, go-live and partnerships. |

## Demeaning competition and commercial defamation

|  |
| --- |
| Negative and unsubstantiated characterization of the competition: liars, garbage, bunkers, hypocrisy, backwardness, phase-out, insecurity, non-compliance, worthless, unreliable. |
| There is no evidence of a derogatory comparison: total crushing, hanging, far more than all peers, the competition is impossible and traditional products are useless. |

| Discrimination and hate speech based on ethnicity, race, religion, gender, geography, disease or disability. |

# Justification required

## Data, statistics, references and impact figures

|  |
| --- |
| High-risk cases: upgrading, growth, reduction, savings, reduction, reduction, reduction, multiplication, accuracy, success rate, conversion rate, coverage, penetration rate, number of clients, number of users, sales volume, market share, satisfaction rate, and any percentage, multiple, ranking and “over X” |
| Use should ensure that: |
| (a) Retroactive raw data or third-party reports; |
| Express data sources, statistical calibres, sample quantities, areas, times and conditions of application; |
| (a) Not to expand the results of single-client, experimental environment or local tests to general effects; |
| The effectiveness data in the client case have been confirmed by the parties concerned, indicating, where necessary, that “actual effects vary according to the client environment”; |
| The data are still valid and the data that have expired or are no longer applicable should be re-checked. |

## Ranking, leadership, initiative and uniqueness

|  |
| --- |
| High-risk cases: leading, global, domestic, industry, leading, head, lead, lead, pole, first, first, first, first, only, exclusive, filling the gap, starting the river, first in the market, first in the ranking. |
| Where it is necessary to use it, both objects, regions, indicators, data sources and deadlines should be limited, and the use of the word “such as” should be avoided in expanding the limited facts to absolute conclusions. |

## Qualifications, awards, patents and partnerships

| Matters | Information |
| --- | --- |
| Qualifications or awards | Use the exact full name of the issuing document to check the issuing body, acquire the subject, the scope of application and the period of validity; no filing, listing or membership may be changed to “accreditation”. |
| Patents | Only authorized and valid patents can be publicized, indicating their number and type; patent promotion may not be authorized in applications or terminated, withdrawn or invalid. |
| Cooperation | “Strategic cooperation” “joint R & D” “official partner” “designated supplier” must have an existing valid written agreement or authorization and must not be expressed beyond the delegated authority. |
| Others rate | Recommendations, certifications and user evaluations must be genuine, with the necessary authorization, and must not be falsified, brushed or selectively edited. |

## Promotion, prices and scarcity

|  |
| --- |
| High-risk cases: original price, flat price, market price, official price, world-wide lowest, historical lowest, factory price, only today, final X, imminent price increase, no longer missed, free of charge, zero, zero cost, one-off, X per cent discount. |
| It must be real and consistent with the transaction page, specifying the duration, number, object, area, conditions of use and range of non-participation; it must not make up the original price, inventory, countdown, sales or winning information. |

## Environmental, low carbon and health effects

|  |
| --- |
| Environmental categories: zero carbon, carbon neutrality, zero emissions, 100 per cent degradability, green, environmentally sound, non-pollution, energy efficiency X per cent with corresponding boundaries, accounting methods, testing or certification. |
| Health category: Non-medical, pharmaceutical or medical equipment advertising may not declare the therapeutic function of disease or use medical terms that can easily be confused with medicines or medical devices. |
| Fuzzy expressions such as “green” “health” should be replaced by specific verifiable attributes, such as materials, energy consumption, emissions, detection indicators or certification ranges. |

# Kuailu HR | FAQ & User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which modules are included? | Employee, Time & Attendance, and Compensation modules are covered in the supplied V1.0 operating manual. |
| Who can operate the system? | HR Specialists and Administrators maintain core data and rules; Department Managers participate in approvals; Employees use self-service workflows. |
| How are employee records created? | Employee master records are primarily generated after pending-onboarding confirmation; HR should not manually create them through the standard Add button. |
| Can shifts be scheduled automatically? | Fixed, Flexible and Free Shift groups can use system scheduling; Scheduled Shift groups require manual scheduling. |
| What happens when a rule or form is approved? | The system writes approved results back to related employee, attendance or compensation records. |
| Are regional rules universal? | No. The supplied manual and sales materials cover different regional contexts. Confirm country rules, statutory calculations and hardware / connectivity constraints for the deployment. |

### Operating sequence

1. Configure organization master data, permissions and workflow automation.
2. Maintain employee records and confirm onboarding workflows.
3. Configure attendance groups, shifts, calendars, rules and leave entitlements.
4. Review attendance forms and reports, then configure compensation rules and payroll periods.
5. Calculate payroll, approve results and distribute payslips according to the configured process.

docs.markdown:
# Attio | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Startups, B2B SaaS, investment and professional services teams, and growing businesses that want to customize objects without heavy traditional CRM. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its main value is AI-native, configurable data model CRM, emphasizing "agentic revenue" and automatic collation of relational data. For the purchaser, this positioning should be mapped to quantifiable issues such as data completeness rate, follow-up timeliness rate, scheduling time, or review completion rate. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | If the needs are mainly sales relations, channels and communication, direct substitution can be evaluated; if the existing system also hosts CPQ, financial, service or complex master data, it should be used as a supplementary layer or phased migration. Not a Hong Kong local payroll tax or local compliance product; complex CPQs, service desks, and large multi-entity governance require verification of packages and integrations. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | Free: $0/user/month for up to 3 seats; Plus: $44 monthly or $35 annual; Pro: $99 monthly or $79 annual; Enterprise: Ask for a quote. AI/workspace credits have quotas, additional packages are added separately. The public price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum number of people, implementation, migration, integration, communication/AI usage, and advanced support shall enter the three-year TCO. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | Need to confirm data residency, cross-border transmission, meeting recording consent, email marketing rules, currency and time zone. CRM claims that GDPR/SOC 2 does not automatically satisfy the Hong Kong PDPO. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | The official customer column shows the use scenarios of multiple teams. The public materials are mainly manufacturer interviews and customer quotes. When purchasing, you should request verifiable performance data of the same size and region. Cases can only prove feasibility leads and cannot replace POCs and customer interviews of the same size, region, and module. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a real sales team to verify email/calendar synchronization, deduplication, opportunity updates, automation, reporting, and export for 2—4 consecutive weeks; record weekly manual maintenance time, missed follow-up rate, and AI costs. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

---

# Clarify | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Founder sales, small B2B teams, and growing companies that want to control costs with AI usage without seats. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its main value is an autonomous CRM billed by AI workload, with sales agents, conference intelligence, automatic archiving, and continuous update transactions at its core. For the purchaser, this positioning should be mapped to quantifiable issues such as data completeness rate, follow-up timeliness rate, scheduling time, or review completion rate. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | If the needs are mainly sales relations, channels and communication, direct substitution can be evaluated; if the existing system also hosts CPQ, financial, service or complex master data, it should be used as a supplementary layer or phased migration. High-frequency conferencing and automation may cause costs to fluctuate with usage; Growth-class SSO, migration, and custom object boundaries need to be confirmed before signing. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | Free: $0/month, unlimited seats, 1,000 credits/month; Starter: $50/month includes 5,000 credits, additional 5,000 credits is $50; Growth: Ask for a quote. Some AI actions are consumed at fixed credits. The public price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum number of people, implementation, migration, integration, communication/AI usage, and advanced support shall enter the three-year TCO. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | Need to confirm data residency, cross-border transmission, meeting recording consent, email marketing rules, currency and time zone. CRM claims that GDPR/SOC 2 does not automatically satisfy the Hong Kong PDPO. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | The public information on the official website focuses on the use of products and pricing calculations. The number of named and quantified customer cases is relatively limited; credits should be measured in real meetings in POC. Cases can only prove feasibility leads and cannot replace POCs and customer interviews of the same size, region, and module. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a real sales team to verify email/calendar synchronization, deduplication, opportunity updates, automation, reporting, and export for 2—4 consecutive weeks; record weekly manual maintenance time, missed follow-up rate, and AI costs. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

# Day AI | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Tech companies and cross-functional GTM teams that want sales, RevOps and AI agents to share customer context. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its primary value is the “customer memory layer” for AI agents, which automatically collects the context of mail, meetings and collaboration and can coexist with established CRMs. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | Direct replacements can be assessed if demand is dominated by sales relationships, pipelines and communications, and if existing systems also contain CPQ, finance, services or complex primary data, they should be either complementary or phased. Not a complete ERP or localised trading system; two-way field with existing CRM, historical backfill range and proxy write permission need to be validated by POC. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | Free: US$ 0/month, 1 user; Turbo: US$ 30/month, or US$ 25/year; Professional: US$ 75/month, or US$ 60/year, inclusive of 10 users; Exective: US$ 250/month, or US$ 200/year, inclusive of 100 users. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | Need to confirm data residency, cross-border transmission, meeting recording consent, email marketing rules, currency and time zone. CRM claims that GDPR/SOC 2 does not automatically satisfy the Hong Kong PDPO. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | User feedback from Score More Sales, Capsule and AdQuick were cited; the quantitative results were limited and the description “20 Minutes of Effect” should be considered as a manufacturer's claim. The case can only prove a path of feasibility and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a real sales team to verify email/calendar synchronization, deduplication, opportunity updates, automation, reporting, and export for 2—4 consecutive weeks; record weekly manual maintenance time, missed follow-up rate, and AI costs. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

# folk | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Agents, founders, recruiting, partners, and relationship-driven teams of around 20—50 people. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | The main value is the collaborative relationship CRM, which integrates contacts, mailboxes, calendars, WhatsApp and LinkedIn workflows into flexible conduits. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | Direct replacements can be assessed if demand is dominated by sales relationships, pipelines and communications, and if existing systems also contain CPQ, finance, services or complex primary data, they should be either complementary or phased. Complex forecasts, CPQs and service management capabilities are weaker than enterprise packages; well-connected, well-informed and AI fields may be limited by credits. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | Standard: $30 per month or $24 per year/member; Premium: $48 per year/member (the corresponding euro price is also displayed in the network); Enterprise starts with $80 per month or $67 per member. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | Need to confirm data residency, cross-border transmission, meeting recording consent, email marketing rules, currency and time zone. CRM claims that GDPR/SOC 2 does not automatically satisfy the Hong Kong PDPO. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | The network has client evaluations and industry articles, but only a limited number of cases are publicly quantified; they should be evaluated over the trial period in a heavy, synchronized and group-based manner. The case can only prove a path of feasibility and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a real sales team to verify email/calendar synchronization, deduplication, opportunity updates, automation, reporting, and export for 2—4 consecutive weeks; record weekly manual maintenance time, missed follow-up rate, and AI costs. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

# Nutshell CRM | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | There is no dedicated administrator, a front-line small and medium-sized enterprise that wishes to move forward quickly with sales and basic marketing. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its primary value is the easy use of CRM for small and medium-sized B2B sales and marketing teams, which includes forms, land pages, chats and AI results quotas. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | Direct replacements can be assessed if demand is dominated by sales relationships, pipelines and communications, and if existing systems also contain CPQ, finance, services or complex primary data, they should be either complementary or phased. High-level privileges, SQL read-only and unlimited pipelines require Enterprise; marketing contacts, text messages, AI outcomes and quote modules increase costs. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | Annual payment per user/month: Foundation $13, Growth 25, Pro 42, Business 59, Enterprise 79; 14 days of trial. Additional fees for marketing, text messaging, Prospector, quotation invoices, etc. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | Need to confirm data residency, cross-border transmission, meeting recording consent, email marketing rules, currency and time zone. CRM claims that GDPR/SOC 2 does not automatically satisfy the Hong Kong PDPO. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | The website publishes a summary of client effectiveness and client evaluation; the data are manufacturer-calibre and provide sample and calculation methods upon request. The case can only prove a viable clue and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a real sales team to verify email/calendar synchronization, deduplication, opportunity updates, automation, reporting, and export for 2—4 consecutive weeks; record weekly manual maintenance time, missed follow-up rate, and AI costs. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

docs.markdown:
# Less Annoying CRM | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Small businesses and individual service providers with approximately 1-50 people, budget sensitive and basic marketing collaboration. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its primary value is the very simple contact and conduit CRM, which provides a single price for small businesses without a set of walls. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | Direct replacements can be assessed if demand is dominated by sales relationships, pipelines and communications, and if existing systems also contain CPQ, finance, services or complex primary data, they should be either complementary or phased. Complex marketing automation, call centres, CPQ or multi-entity governance are not appropriate; API and advanced ecological capabilities need to be identified on a case-by-case basis. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | $15/user/month, monthly, no contract, no set-up; 30 days full functionality trial. Officially, all upgrades are included in the same price. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | Need to confirm data residency, cross-border transmission, meeting recording consent, email marketing rules, currency and time zone. CRM claims that GDPR/SOC 2 does not automatically satisfy the Hong Kong PDPO. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | The network includes small business evaluations and comparisons, but there is a lack of large-scale quantitative implementation cases; it is suitable for a 30-day trial of direct validation. The case can only prove a viable clue and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a real sales team to verify email/calendar synchronization, deduplication, opportunity updates, automation, reporting, and export for 2—4 consecutive weeks; record weekly manual maintenance time, missed follow-up rate, and AI costs. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

---

# SugarCRM | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | There are large and medium-sized organizations with structured marketing processes, 15 or more seats, industry customization and corporate governance. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its primary value is a sales, marketing and service platform for medium-sized and large B2B enterprises, with emphasis on configuration processes, forecasting and deployment controls. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | Direct replacements can be assessed if demand is dominated by sales relationships, pipelines and communications, and if existing systems also contain CPQ, finance, services or complex primary data, they should be either complementary or phased. 15 User start-up and implementation services raise small team thresholds; AI, LinkedIn connectors, storage and support borders vary from version to version. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | Sugar Sell pays and at least 15 users annually: Standard $59, Advanced $85, Premier $135/user/month; Sugar Enterprise $85, Enterprise + 120. Market starts with $1,000/month/10,000 contacts. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | Need to confirm data residency, cross-border transmission, meeting recording consent, email marketing rules, currency and time zone. CRM claims that GDPR/SOC 2 does not automatically satisfy the Hong Kong PDPO. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | Official information includes client quotations and cases such as Agriconomie; all results should be verified by deployment, number of users and additional purchase module. The case can only prove a path of feasibility and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a real sales team to verify email/calendar synchronization, deduplication, opportunity updates, automation, reporting, and export for 2—4 consecutive weeks; record weekly manual maintenance time, missed follow-up rate, and AI costs. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

# Vtiger | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Small, medium and medium-sized enterprises that wish to reduce multiple applications and mix licences between standard users and single application users. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its primary value is the full functionality of CRM, which consolidates sales, marketing, services, projects and inventory views, and provides an AI version. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | Direct replacements can be assessed if demand is dominated by sales relationships, pipelines and communications, and if existing systems also contain CPQ, finance, services or complex primary data, they should be either complementary or phased. The breadth of the module may result in configuration complexity; AI and advanced privileges are in high brackets; local compliance and finance need to be integrated accordingly. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | Standard annual payment users: One Growth $12, Professional $30, Enterprise 42, One AI 50/user/month; People over Professional can purchase a lower price list application. One Pilot is free of charge for up to 10 users. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | Need to confirm data residency, cross-border transmission, meeting recording consent, email marketing rules, currency and time zone. CRM claims that GDPR/SOC 2 does not automatically satisfy the Hong Kong PDPO. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | The official network provides client stories and industry programmes; the assessment needs to distinguish between the one edition and the old one of Sales CRM and avoid applying inconsistent cases. The case can only prove a path of feasibility and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a real sales team to verify email/calendar synchronization, deduplication, opportunity updates, automation, reporting, and export for 2—4 consecutive weeks; record weekly manual maintenance time, missed follow-up rate, and AI costs. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Hotels, restaurants, retail sales, nursing and other multi-site line industries. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its main values are integrated labour management, remuneration and hosting remuneration platforms for shifts and hours. | How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | Prices are customized for monthly active staff, selected modules and areas; monthly subscriptions, officially not required for long-term lockouts. The software remuneration is a different package from that of hosting. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | There is a need to verify labour rules, wage calculations, statutory forms, data presence and support time zones on a regional basis; “multi-country support” is not equivalent to a declaration of primary pay per country. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |

| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

# BridgeBuilder HRMS | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Hong Kong ' s large and medium-sized enterprises, trans-Hong Kong Mainland and South-East Asia operate retail, hotel and service groups. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its main value is the HRMS of Hong Kong under the flag of FlexSystem, which is implemented for complex local pay, vacation time and Asia and the Pacific. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | The replacement of the core HRIS depends on remuneration, statutory filing, master data and interface coverage. High customization may increase the cost of implementation and upgrading; “compliance” should be finally confirmed by the employer/legal adviser; and cross-border coverage needs to be validated country by country. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | The network uses customized offers based on modules, numbers, areas, cloud/local deployments, interfaces and customizations; typical projects are also subject to implementation, relocation, parallel payroll and training budgets. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | There is a need to verify labour rules, wage calculations, statutory forms, data presence and support time zones on a regional basis; “multi-country support” is not equivalent to a declaration of primary pay per country. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | In the case of official names, Louis Vuitton North Asia covered the Mainland of Hong Kong for four months and was close to 50 per cent of the salary; there was also angnès b. and EC Healthcare. All were manufacturer cases and the project calibre should be verified. The case can only prove a path of feasibility and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a department or location to run a full cycle to validate employee data, clearance, time off/performance or recruitment; in the case of remuneration, complete at least one parallel pay and difference reconciliation. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | The replacement of the core HRIS depends on remuneration, statutory filing, master data and interface coverage. Cross-border remuneration, complex group competencies and large-scale interfaces need to be confirmed; some of the information is released earlier, based on current demonstrations and contracts. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | The official brochure describes the different fees and technical support plans provided according to the needs of the enterprise, the price of which requires contact with the client manager; and the budget requires reconciliation of the staff billing, modules, implementation and support levels. | What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | There is a need to verify labour rules, wage calculations, statutory forms, data presence and support time zones on a regional basis; “multi-country support” is not equivalent to a declaration of primary pay per country. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | The information on the Open Office Network is based on functional and ecological descriptions and lacks detailed quantitative cases that can be independently verified; cooperation Logo should not be directly presented as a success story. | When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Largely staffed, multi-legalized, enterprise groups wishing to unify HR, pay, talent and staff experience. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its primary value is HCM, a business that covers the entire life cycle of Hire-to-ReHire, with a focus on India, the Middle East, Africa and South-East Asia. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | The replacement of the core HRIS depends on remuneration, statutory filing, master data and interface coverage. The local payroll tax in Hong Kong is not the focus of the network and must be validated on a case-by-case basis; large-scale data migration, change management and local partner capacity are key risks. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | The standard subscription price for the network is not open and is based on the number of employees, country, module, implementation and service request; the price boundary between zero contact pay and hosting services should be separately identified. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | There is a need to verify labour rules, wage calculations, statutory forms, data presence and support time zones on a regional basis; “multi-country support” is not equivalent to a declaration of primary pay per country. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | The network names 1,200+ enterprises, 2.8 million active users and displays large clients; the percentage of functional effectiveness is the manufacturer ' s claim that the customer should be required to certify the material. The case can only prove a path of feasibility and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a department or location to run a full cycle to validate employee data, clearance, time off/performance or recruitment; in the case of remuneration, complete at least one parallel pay and difference reconciliation. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

# Keka | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | Indian and international growth enterprises, especially organizations that provide IT services, professional services and require HR+PSA. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its primary value is an integrated, staff experience-oriented platform for HR, remuneration, recruitment, performance and project hours. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | The replacement of the core HRIS depends on remuneration, statutory filing, master data and interface coverage. Local remuneration and taxation in Hong Kong are not core evidence; global prices are not transparent; and the permitted boundaries between modules such as PSA, ATS and the base HCM need to be confirmed. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | The official network displays food packages such as Foundation, Strangth and free trials, but the current page does not disclose a global flat amount that can be directly accounted for; prices are quoted by region, staff and module. Overuse and additional modules may be accounted for separately. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | There is a need to verify labour rules, wage calculations, statutory forms, data presence and support time zones on a regional basis; “multi-country support” is not equivalent to a declaration of primary pay per country. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | The Network describes the use of 12,500+ as well as the publication of the WorldIndia, Traveazy and others; the manufacturer's materials require verification of the regional version and scope of implementation. The case can only prove a path of feasibility and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a department or location to run a full cycle to validate employee data, clearance, time off/performance or recruitment; in the case of remuneration, complete at least one parallel pay and difference reconciliation. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |
