# Zoho Recruit | Core QA User Guide

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Which organization is it best for? | From a single recruiter to an enterprise or recruitment agency requiring a high degree of self-definition, automation and Zoho integration. |
| What is the primary problem it solves? | Its main values are ATS in the Zoho ecology and the recruitment of CRMs, which are available in enterprise HR and recruitment agency versions. For the procurement party, this location should be mapped to quantifiable issues, such as data integrity, follow-up timeliness, scheduling time or evaluation completion. |
| Is it possible to replace the existing core system? | The replacement of the core HRIS depends on remuneration, statutory filing, master data and interface coverage. The layout and regional prices are more complex; AI, portal, field security is at the top; not core HR/remuneration, and candidate privacy and retention rules need to be configured. |
| How should AI and automation be evaluated? | Don't just watch the demo. Verify with 20—50 real records or one full cycle: input source, recommendation accuracy, manual review points, permissions, failure rollbacks, dosage costs, and audit records. |
| How do you understand public pricing? | Enterprise HR editions include Free, Standard, Enterprise; US help page listing Standard $30/user/month, with different regional and annual/monthly rates. The recruitment agency version is also available. On a 15-day trial basis, video interviews, staff permits, additional positions and senior support may be acquired. The open price is only the software entrance, and taxes, minimum numbers, implementation, migration, integration, communications/AI usage and advanced support should enter the TCO for three years. |
| What should I pay attention to when using it in Hong Kong or across regions? | There is a need to verify labour rules, wage calculations, statutory forms, data presence and support time zones on a regional basis; “multi-country support” is not equivalent to a declaration of primary pay per country. |
| What are the integration priorities? | Priority checks for authentication, mail/calendar or attendance devices, master data direction, API limits, webhooks, error retries, field mappings, historical backfill, and delete synchronization. The "presence" of the interface does not mean that the real-time and governance requirements are met. |
| What is the typical implementation complexity? | Lightweight ranges can be imported and launched with standard templates first; once multi-entity, historical data, complex permissions, bi-directional integration, or statutory calculations are involved, design, cleaning, UAT, parallel operation, training, and post-launch support phases should be set up. |
| What is the minimum safety due diligence question? | Request the latest audit/certification, DPA, subcontractor list, data location, encryption, backup and recovery, RTO/RPO, SSO/SCIM, logs, deletion export mechanism, AI training policy and event notification terms. |
| Can the customer case directly prove the effect? | According to the official network, 800,000 professionals were recruited to use and display Logo, such as Stellantis, Bosch, Deloitte and others; Logo did not specify the food package or its effects, but requested specific cases. The case can only prove a path of feasibility and cannot be a substitute for interviews with clients on the same scale, in the same area, with the modular POC. |
| What is the recommended POC? | Select a department or location to run a full cycle to validate employee data, clearance, time off/performance or recruitment; in the case of remuneration, complete at least one parallel pay and difference reconciliation. |
| When is it not recommended? | If critical requirements fall outside its boundaries, contract-level safety/compliance evidence cannot be provided, migration and exit scenarios are unclear, or three-year TCO is out of control with real usage, it is not advisable to procure solely because of the interface or AI demo. |

---

# CRM Industry Core Conclusions

| Dimension | Current knowledge |
| --- | --- |
| Industry role | CRM is the system of record for customer identity, relationships, marketing, sales, service, channel collaboration and revenue analysis. It is broader than a contact directory or a lead list. |
| Best-fit demand | High-value B2B sales with long cycles, repeated follow-up, complex quotations and a need to connect ERP, finance or order data. |
| Priority segments | Export manufacturing, industrial distribution and cross-border B2B are the first priority segments; B2B software/services and international logistics are secondary segments. |
| Market stage | CRM is moving from customer records and sales-process digitisation toward unified data, AI-assisted decisions and AI-executed workflows. |
| Data boundary | Industry economic indicators are proxy indicators for the customer pool, not CRM SaaS TAM. CRM, CRM SaaS and sales-force-automation figures use different statistical scopes. |
| Compliance baseline | Customer data, marketing outreach, profiling, AI-generated content and cross-border transfers require purpose limitation, permissions, consent or another lawful basis, auditability and user controls. |
| Durable opportunity | Industry workflows, AI execution, quotation/order/collection linkage, data quality, compliant cross-border outreach and low-complexity deployment are more defensible than an AI label alone. |

# CRM Technology Architecture & Data Flow

| Layer | Required capability | Control point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data foundation | Account, contact, product, price, opportunity, order and collection master data | Deduplication, ownership, field standards and change history |
| Experience layer | Web, mobile, email, meeting and supported communication entry points | Identity, consent and channel authorisation |
| AI layer | Retrieval, summarisation, recommendation, extraction and task execution | Model scope, confidence thresholds, prompt-injection protection and human approval |
| Workflow layer | Lead assignment, follow-up, stage movement, quotation and approval | Role permissions, segregation of duties and rollback |
| Integration layer | ERP, finance, marketing, messaging and order systems | API authentication, mapping, retry, reconciliation and rate limits |
| Evidence layer | Activity, decision, export and integration logs | Retention, audit search and incident review |

# CRM Deployment & Integration

| Deployment concern | Practical requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Tenant and identity | Separate customer tenants, define role-based access and reclaim ownership when a salesperson leaves. |
| Master data | Establish canonical identifiers for accounts, contacts, products, price lists, orders and payments before synchronisation. |
| Connector scope | Confirm target ERP, finance, marketing, email, messaging and order interfaces; do not infer integration from a product label alone. |
| Regional operation | Support time zones, languages, currencies, data residency and country-specific outreach controls where required. |
| Change management | Start with one sales workflow and measurable POC outcomes, then expand connectors and automation after reconciliation is stable. |
| Audit and recovery | Keep operation logs, approval history, data-export records and a rollback path for high-risk AI writes. |

# CRM Laws & Compliance Requirements

| Jurisdiction | Requirement relevant to CRM operations |
| --- | --- |
| Mainland China | PIPL requires a lawful basis, purpose limitation and appropriate protection for customer and contact data. Automated marketing should offer a non-personalised option or a convenient refusal mechanism. |
| Mainland China | Network data rules require safeguards such as encryption, backup, access control and security authentication. |
| Mainland China | Cross-border transfers need a separate assessment. Data that contains personal information cannot be treated as ordinary enterprise data, even when used for international trade. |
| European Union | GDPR requires a lawful basis, transparency, data-subject rights, retention controls and safeguards for profiling or significant automated decisions. |
| United States | CAN-SPAM requires accurate sender information, a physical postal address and a clear, working opt-out mechanism for commercial email. AI-generated voice outreach may also trigger TCPA requirements. |
| Singapore and ASEAN | PDPA and the Do Not Call Registry affect collection, use, disclosure and marketing outreach. ASEAN AI guidance supports a common responsible-AI baseline but does not replace national laws. |
| Product control | Maintain consent/lawful-basis tags, source records, suppression lists, regional rules, export logs, retention settings and human approval for high-risk actions. |

# HR Technology Architecture & Data Flow

| Layer | Required capability | Control point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workforce master | Employee, position, organisation, site, contract and payroll-rule data | Unique identity, effective dates, transfer history and tenant isolation |

| Workflow layer | Recruitment, onboarding, attendance exceptions, approvals and payroll closing | Role permissions, separation of duties and versioned rules |
| Attendance layer | Mobile, site, shift, overtime, leave and exception capture | Necessity, minimisation, alternative verification and device controls |
| Payroll layer | Salary components, tax, social insurance and regional rules | Effective-date versioning, reconciliation and payslip auditability |

# HR Deployment & Integration

| Deployment concern | Practical requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Organisation model | Support multiple companies, sites, departments, roles, shifts and effective-date changes without flattening the hierarchy. |
| Payroll rules | Configure region, role, allowance, overtime, tax and social-insurance rules with version history; do not hard-code one national template. |
| Device and attendance | Confirm mobile, biometric, card, location and alternative verification methods; use the least intrusive method that meets the business purpose. |
| System connections | Confirm finance, ERP, identity, attendance-device, tax and social-insurance interfaces; capability names do not guarantee a connector. |
| Data governance | Restrict salary, identity, performance and biometric fields by role, retain administrator logs and remove access promptly after departure. |
| Rollout method | Start with one site or business unit, reconcile employee and payroll masters, then expand to additional sites and countries. |

# HR Laws & Compliance Requirements

| Jurisdiction | Requirement relevant to HR operations |
| --- | --- |
| Mainland China | PIPL requires a lawful basis and appropriate protection for employee information. HR processing under labour rules or collective agreements must still follow necessity, transparency and security duties. |
| Mainland China | Significant automated HR decisions require fairness, explanation and a human review or appeal path. AI screening should assist rather than silently determine hiring outcomes. |
| Mainland China | The 2024 cross-border data rules provide a conditional HR-management route for certain employee transfers, but do not remove other PIPL obligations. |
| Mainland China | Face-recognition rules effective 1 June 2025 emphasise necessity and minimisation; non-biometric attendance options should remain available where they can achieve the same purpose. |
| Mainland China | Personal-information compliance audits effective 1 May 2025 make data maps, access history and audit exports valuable for larger processors. Labour, social-insurance, tax, wage and working-time rules require regional and effective-date versioning. |
| European Union | GDPR and the EU AI Act treat employment and recruitment AI as a high-governance area; maintain data governance, logs, technical documentation and human oversight ahead of the relevant 2027 high-risk obligations. |
| United States | Federal rules are supplemented by anti-discrimination enforcement and local requirements such as New York City’s automated employment decision-tool rules. |
| Singapore and ASEAN | PDPA and regional responsible-AI guidance support privacy, accountability and explainability; country-specific employment and data requirements still apply. |
